messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into Malayalam, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE Malayalam line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG] After the table, list any MISSING or WRONG items.

### Missing / Problematic Items - **che** (comparative subordinator) – not rendered explicitly in Malayalam. - **ch'i'** (first occurrence) – relative pronoun omitted; the clause is fused into the participial form **കണ്ടെത്തിയ**. - **ch'i'** (second occurrence) – same issue; the relative pronoun is absorbed in **കണ്ട**. - **v'ho** – auxiliary “have” of the perfect is not expressed separately in Malayalam; the perfect aspect is conveyed by the past participle **കണ്ട**.
All other source tokens have appropriate Malayalam equivalents and are marked **OK**.

### Step 4: Correction & Final Output Fix any MISSING or WRONG items from Step 3. Reorder within line if needed; do not add new content words. Output per line: Line #, Original Translation, Issues, Corrected Translation (if any). Output final Malayalam text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).
